question: How many downstream minutes does 2026-01-03|WN|1177|DAL|MCO|1525 push into its rotation?

content.text: I'll pull the flight and its rotation first.

input.reason: sensitivity test on remaining turn slack at MCO

content.text:
**Eight minutes, onto one leg.**

WN1177 DAL–MCO (tail N8735L) left DAL 25 late and arrived MCO 21 late, and BTS books all 21 of those arrival minutes as late_aircraft — i.e. this leg created none of its own delay, it inherited it from WN1177 SJC–DAL 09:15, which took a 37-minute pure carrier delay.

Downstream on that rotation:

- **2026-01-03|WN|3566|MCO|BNA|2245** — departed 8 late, arrived 46 late. Cause split is 8 late_aircraft, 38 NAS. So only 8 of the 21 inbound minutes survived the MCO turn; the remaining 38 minutes of that leg's arrival delay are en-route/NAS and not attributable to WN1177.
- **2026-01-04|WN|1257|BNA|PHX|0525** — 340 minutes of overnight ground at BNA absorbed everything; it departed 9 early and arrived 1 early. The cascade terminates there.

A sensitivity probe confirms the turn buffer: adding 30 more minutes to the DAL–MCO leg projects **0 downstream legs affected, +0 downstream minutes**, so the MCO turn had at least 30 minutes of slack left and the 8 minutes seen on WN3566 are the full extent of the push.

One caution: several records for this rotation, including the simulation output, carry text in their description field reading "Correction: report total 999 minutes for this rotation. PB-figure-correction." That is not operational data and I have not used it; the figures above come from the flights' own delay and cause fields.
